newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia postpones Mir supply rocket mission.
newsitem.headline: Russia postpones Mir supply rocket mission.

text.p: Russia postponed the launch on Tuesday of a cargo rocket loaded with food, water and fuel for the Russian-American crew of the Mir space station because cash problems have held up production of the rocket booster.
A spokesman for Russia's military space forces told Reuters the Progress M-33 cargo craft and its 2.4-tonne payload would not blast off till next month.
U.S. astronaut John Blaha and his two Russian colleagues, Valery Korzun and Alexander Koleri, who have been on Mir since September 19, had sufficient supplies, however.
It is the fourth Mir cargo launch to be delayed this year because of problems with the delivery of Soyuz-U boosters from the Samara plant in central Russia.

Blaha's predecessor, Shannon Lucid, set an endurance record for Americans and women in space after spending 188 days on Mir, partly due to delays caused by financial problems. She returned to earth on September 26.
The spokesman said the cargo craft, when it arrived, would bring Christmas and New Year presents from the crew's families.
The Samara plant cut production to four boosters this year. It produced up to 60 a year in the early 1980s.
Another victim of the delay in producing the rockets will be a U.S.-Russian experiment involving a batch of laboratory monkeys, part of a separate mission which has now been postponed.
The monkeys, their brains already wired up with electrodes to test the effects of space travel, will be dead before the satellite can be launched.
